title: fix(mcp): a coded refusal reaches the client with its code on the data tools, list_actions and the record resource
body:
Fixes #23509

Clause-②: yes

## What changes

The MCP data tools rendered a thrown refusal with `errorResult(messageOf(err))`: `list_objects`, `describe_object`, `validate_expression`, `query_records`, `aggregate_records`, `get_record`, `create_record`, `update_record` and `delete_record`. So did `list_actions`. The record resource `objectstack://objects/{objectName}/records/{recordId}` wrote `{ error: message }`.

So when a producer threw the ADR-0112 envelope, an MCP client received the message and nothing else. The code is the machine-readable half the client acts on, and it was lost for every coded refusal on these surfaces:

- a held owner's key, `MFA_REQUIRED`. Ruling C′ on #23287, item 1: "a held user's API key is refused at every seam with the same code";
- `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`;
- `PERMISSION_DENIED`;
- `INVALID_FIELD`;
- the exposure refusals.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`**

- The 10 catches now return `errorResultWithCode(err)`. It renders `{ error: { code, message, status } }`, the shape `run_action` already answers with (chosen for the action tools in #15942), but **without `details`**. The section below explains why.
- `run_action` and `resume_run` keep `errorResultFromThrown`. Their text is byte-identical: same members, same key order.
- Both renderers read the throw through one function, `thrownRefusalEnvelope(err)`. It is a named export of the module and is not re-exported from the package index.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`**

- The record resource's catch adds `code`, and `status` when the refusal carries one, beside the unchanged `error` sentence.

**Unchanged**

- A throw with no non-empty string `code` renders exactly as today on both surfaces.
- No code is minted. No refusal's message changes.

### FROM → TO: what an MCP client reads

| surface | refusal | FROM | TO |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| the 9 data tools and `list_actions` | coded | `isError: true`; the text is the message | `isError: true`; the text is the JSON `{ "error": { "code", "message", "status" } }`. `status` appears only when the refusal carries one. |
| record resource (stdio) | coded | `{ "error": MESSAGE }` | `{ "error": MESSAGE, "code", "status" }`. `status` appears only when the refusal carries one. `error` is the same string as before. |
| either | no code | the message | unchanged, byte-identical |

### Why `details` is withheld

I measured it at the real `/mcp` door, on the showcase stack with security enabled. A `PERMISSION_DENIED` thrown by the security gate (`plugin-security` `security-plugin.ts`, the denial with `positions` / `permissionSets`) reaches the tool catch carrying the caller's `positions` (`org_member`, `everyone`) and `permissionSets` (`showcase_member_default`, `member_default`) in `details`.

The runtime dispatcher drops those `details` from the wire. Its catch in `http-dispatcher.ts` reads "The denial's `details` does NOT reach the wire" and records the ruling on #7450.

That policy lives in `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-security`, and neither is a dependency of this package. So these surfaces serve the members every boundary serves: `code`, `message` and `status`. The card's done line asks for exactly that: "with its `code` (and `status` where the envelope carries one)".

The first revision of this branch rendered `details`. The real-door probe caught the disclosure, and the head commit removes it. Ten pins plus an ablation now hold the withholding (below).

### Why the record resource keeps a flat shape

The tools take `errorResultFromThrown`'s nesting. The resource takes the same members but not the nesting: it answers `{ error: MESSAGE, code, status }`, not `{ error: { code, message, status } }`. Three reasons:

- The two sibling resources already answer in this flat vocabulary. `objectstack://objects/{objectName}` answers `{ error, code, status }` on a miss or an outage (#6055), and `objectstack://objects` answers the same pair on a degraded listing (#6504).
- Two existing readers in this package tell a refusal from a row by `typeof body.error === 'string'`. One is the normalizer in `plugin.record-resource-exposure.test.ts`; the other is the member case in `stdio-data-bridge.stored-metadata-body.test.ts`. A nested `error` object would turn their refusal branch into "this is a row". That would be a narrowing on a surface this PR declares as a widening.
- The dispatch scope for the resource ("carries the `code`, and the `status` where the envelope has one") is met either way.

## Faces

- **stdio** serves the tools and the record resource. `MFA_REQUIRED` is pinned on both, over a real `StdioServerTransport`.
- **HTTP `/mcp`** serves the tools only. `handleHttpRequest` registers no resources: the record resource exists only on the long-lived server (`plugin.ts:738`).
  - A held key is refused at the dispatcher before the MCP server sees it. That is the dispatch's mechanism note, and I did not re-measure it. So the HTTP pins use refusals that do reach the tool catch.
  - Measured at the real door (`POST /api/v1/mcp`, showcase stack, a member caller), on the final head:
    - `get_record` and `update_record` on another owner's row: `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` / 404;
    - `delete_record`: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403, with no `details`;
    - `create_record` with an unknown field and `query_records` filtering on one: `INVALID_FIELD` / 400.
  - Each answered `isError: true` with `{ error: { code, message, status } }`.
  - The probe was a temporary file, deleted after the run and never committed.

## Tests re-judged (none loosened, none deleted)

| test | refusal it pins | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `stdio-api-key-account-posture.pin.test.ts` (#23508's real-transport pin) | `MFA_REQUIRED` / 403, coded | **moved to the coded rendering.** `tools/call query_records` now asserts `{ error: { code: 'MFA_REQUIRED', message, status: 403 } }`; it asserted the text equal to the message. Extended with `resources/read` on the record over the same wire: `{ error: message, code: 'MFA_REQUIRED', status: 403 }`. |
| `plugin.record-resource-exposure.test.ts`, the `apiEnabled: false` and the whitelist-excludes-`get` cases | `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / 404, `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` / 405, coded | **moved.** The normalizer reads the code and status from both wires. The cases still assert the same sentence on both paths, and now also the code and status. |
| `stdio-data-bridge.relation-condition-target-exposure.test.ts`, the `query_records` tool case | `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / 404, coded | **moved.** It stayed green as a substring inside the JSON, so it was re-judged rather than left as is. It now parses the envelope and asserts the code, the status and both message fragments. |
| `mcp-server-runtime.http.test.ts` (`RLS: not permitted`, `Field read denied`) | plain `Error`, no code | **code-less**, unchanged |
| `mcp-action-tools.test.ts` (`list_actions`: `metadata unavailable`) | plain `Error`, no code | **code-less**, unchanged |
| `mcp-action-confirmation-member.test.ts` (`handler exploded`) | plain `Error`, no code | **code-less**, unchanged |
| `mcp-validate-expression.test.ts` (`not found`), `mcp-resume-run-tool.test.ts` (`runId is required`), every `system object` case | an `errorResult` literal, never a throw | not a thrown refusal, unchanged |
| `stdio-data-bridge.stored-metadata-body.test.ts`, the member case | reads `typeof body.error === 'string'` | holds under the flat shape, unchanged |

## Pins added: `packages/mcp/src/mcp-coded-refusal.test.ts` (42 cases)

- **HTTP face, every registered tool.** The pins run through the real Streamable HTTP transport, one row per tool, each driven by its own bridge member. The table is held equal to `tools/list`, so a tool added later needs a row.
  - The real `recordNotFoundError` renders as `{ error: { code: 'RECORD_NOT_FOUND', message, status: 404 } }` with `isError`.
  - A code-less `Error` renders as its bare message, byte-identical.
  - On the 10 rows other than `run_action` and `resume_run`, the security gate's `PERMISSION_DENIED` renders as code, message and status, and the `details` are withheld.
- **Boundaries.**
  - The HTTP bridge's exposure gate throws `{ statusCode, message }` with no `code`; it renders as the bare message, so nothing is invented.
  - An empty or numeric `code`, or a thrown string, is not a code.
  - A non-numeric `status` is omitted.
- **Record resource.**
  - `MFA_REQUIRED` renders as `{ error, code, status }`.
  - `PERMISSION_DENIED` renders as code and status, with `details` withheld.
  - A refusal with no `status` gets no `status`.
  - A code-less throw answers `{ error }` byte-identically.

## Ablation (one-time; nothing committed)

All three legs ran on the final code. Each went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit once, the blob changed, and the restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The subject resolves through relative `src/` imports, not a dependency's `dist/`, so no rebuild leg applies. Every leg turned red, the expected direction.

1. **`query_records`' catch reverted to `errorResult(messageOf(err))`.** Blob `b7a491d6641b → 6c8a41093f41`. **4 red:**
   - the `query_records` `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` row;
   - the `query_records` `PERMISSION_DENIED` row;
   - the non-numeric-status row;
   - the stdio `MFA_REQUIRED` pin.

   The code-less row stayed green, as it should. Restored to `b7a491d6641b`.
2. **`errorResultWithCode` made to carry `details`.** Blob `b7a491d6641b → f80698dd3e44`. **10 red:** every `WITHHOLDS its details` row. Nothing else went red. Restored.
3. **The record resource's envelope read disabled.** Blob `3ef6ce641eb8 → 65c81c69b058`. **6 red:**
   - the stdio `MFA_REQUIRED` resource read;
   - the three coded resource rows;
   - both #8266 parity cases.

   The code-less resource row stayed green. Restored.

`mcp-http-tools.ts` is byte-identical between the head of legs 1 and 2 and the final head (`b7a491d6641b`). The merge of `main` touched no `packages/mcp` file.

## Verification

All at `6c70ec74ab`.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp test`: **38 files, 462 tests passed**, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. That is 420 before this PR plus 42 new; the three coded pins that asserted the message alone were moved, not deleted.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit` passes, and `check:test-typecheck: OK`. The 53 errors it reports are the ones held in the shrink-only debt ledger, and none is in a touched file. All four touched test files are in the `tsconfig.test.json` program, counted with `--listFiles`.
- Dependency closure: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/mcp^...' build` exited 0. After the merge of `main`, `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/dogfood^...'` ran 65/65 tasks.
- Consumer tests that read MCP tool output, run on the final head: `packages/qa/dogfood` `showcase-mcp-http-identity`, `flow-door-elevated-start`, `showcase-mcp-self-connection` and `showcase-declarative-mcp`, plus the temporary real-door probe. **5 files, 39 tests passed.**
- `packages/cli/test/package-install-local-handlers.integration.test.ts` reads only `run_action` and a successful `list_actions`, paths this PR does not change. It is integration tier and declared to CI.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 63 families from the change set. I ran all 63 locally on this head and each exited 0. The `--ran` reconciliation, fed `command :: exit code` lines, reads: "63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", a zero derived from the recorded codes.
  - Verdict lines include `check-adr-0087-registration: this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset (1 non-breaking changeset(s) seen)`, `No empty-frontmatter changeset introduced by this diff`, `check-nul-bytes: OK`, `doc authoring guard: … clean`, `check-test-source-alias OK`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads — 110 published require entry point(s) across 68 package(s) load` and `check-lean-entry-closure: 2 published condition(s) measured`.
  - In an earlier round on a superseded head, the last two answered exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because a concurrent build was rewriting `dist/`. They were re-run and are exit 0 on this head.
- The repo-wide scans, with `pnpm lint` first, and the rest of the farm run in CI.

## Acceptance notes

Two findings go to the seat in this PR's report and are not filed from here:

1. **On `/mcp`, the bridge's exposure refusal carries no code.**
   - `callData`'s gate on the addressed object (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:304`) throws `{ statusCode, message }` with no `code`, and `buildMcpBridge` calls `callData` for every `/mcp` data verb.
   - So after this PR, `get_record` / `query_records` on an object declaring `apiEnabled: false` still renders the message alone on `/mcp`. That case is pinned as code-less here: nothing is invented.
   - The stdio face (`enforceApiExposure`) and REST (`rest-server.ts:510`) answer `OBJECT_API_DISABLED`, and so does the same `callData`'s relation-target refusal.
   - The fix belongs at that producer, in `packages/runtime`, not in this consumer.
2. **`run_action` / `resume_run` render `details` verbatim** through `errorResultFromThrown` (#15942's contract, unchanged here).
   - `resume_run`'s errors are built through the REST error builder.
   - `run_action` loads its subject record through `callData` as the caller. If a security-gate `PERMISSION_DENIED` escapes it, its `positions` / `permissionSets` would reach the MCP client, while the dispatcher withholds them.
   - I have not measured this path.

Observations, not filed:

- The AI tool-registry bridge's catch (`registerToolFromDefinition` in `mcp-server-runtime.ts`) also renders a throw as its message alone. No coded producer was measured on that path.
- Members beside `code` / `message` / `status` are not rendered on these surfaces: the stdio 405's `allowedOperations`, and the runtime refusal's `allowed`, `object` and `param`. REST's 405 carries `allowed`.
- A refusal's `details` could help an AI self-correct, for example a validation error's field list. Serving them would need the per-class disclosure policy this package does not hold. Nothing pulls on it today.
